name: Certified Information Systems Auditor

fee.note: US$575 for ISACA members (membership is a separate purchase). Certification adds a one-time US$50 application fee after passing, then a yearly maintenance fee of US$45 (members) or US$85 (non-members).

exam.format: 150 multiple-choice questions in 4 hours, at a PSI test centre or remotely proctored, in English, Chinese, Spanish, Japanese, French, German or Korean. Registration opens a six-month window to sit the exam. Scores are scaled; pretest items are not scored.

scope: Auditing information systems: the audit process, IT governance and management, systems acquisition and implementation, operations and business resilience, and protection of information assets.
requirements: Anyone can sit the exam. To be certified: five or more years of professional information systems auditing, control or security work experience, gained within the 10 years before applying; ISACA's candidate guide allows waivers for up to three of those years. Apply within five years of passing, pay the US$50 application fee and follow ISACA's Code of Professional Ethics, CPE policy and IS auditing standards.
ai_policy: Check the current assessment rules. AI-assisted study does not imply permission during the exam.
caveats: The current outline has applied since 1 August 2024; ISACA had not announced a newer CISA outline on its pages as of 2026-11-17.

Validity is yearly: ISACA renews the certification each calendar year with the maintenance fee and at least 20 CPE hours, and 120 over each three-year cycle. From 1 January 2027 at least 90 of those 120 hours must align with the exam content outline.
Up to four attempts in a rolling 12 months (waits of 30, 90 and 90 days), each paid in full.
